title: Duduk
summary: Rendered, not graded: no licensed recording of this duduk is in the library, and the screened duduk clips are YouTube all-rights-reserved listening references, so no recording sits beside a note. The card is the A duduk of Maugeais and Dalmont 2024 (Acta Acustica 8, article 60, CC BY 4.0): body 354 mm, a plain 12 mm bore of 0.442 m from the reed tip, ten 9.0 mm holes measured from their Figure 1 (the text says only that the holes are of one size, +-0.5 mm; undercut not modelled), the first k holes closed per their Table 1, the authors' lumped reed (resonance 480 Hz and quality factor 3.3, both FITTED by the authors to this duduk; closing pressure 4500 Pa, opening 0.3 mm), the reed pressure face S_r = 1.08e-4 m2 (w x Lr = 0.018 x 0.006 of the authors' own online simulator, whose code and not the paper's print holds it; whether the 6 mm is measured or chosen is not stated), blown at 2250 Pa = 0.5 Pcr in saturated breath at 300.15 K; 11 fingerings are lowered, four are rendered. The reed interior is the open item, and the bracket is one line: Fig 6 round interior 22.07 cm3 = 250-450 c flat; linear-flattened 8.83 cm3 = 88-348 c sharp; the plain 12 mm bore 11.65 cm3 used here. The first two readings of the impedance check failed in opposite directions, and the plain bore was chosen after that check (its first peaks lie -27 to +55 cents of the authors' values at 293.15 K dry air and carry none of their high-register inharmonicity: the second peak is 62, 134 and 191 cents sharp of 3 f1 at A, B+1 and C+1 for the authors, -44, -26 and -10 here). A measured section b(x) of the flattened reed interior would settle it; the authors' data is stated to be available on request. Played fundamental of each render (steady 1.0 to 2.3 s, one binary, S_r 1x) beside the first peak printed in the legend of their Figure 7 (a passive peak of their hybrid impedance, not a played pitch; D has no legend peak, the value is derived from their public simulator, https://perso.univ-lemans.fr/~smauge/Acoustics/yapsmi.js/instruments/duduk/) and beside the passive impedance peak of the same card in the render's own bore gas (speed of sound 345.36 m/s): G-1: legend 180.8 Hz, passive peak 184.94 Hz, played 172.82 Hz (-78.1 c from the legend, -117.3 c from the passive peak); D: simulator 279.13 Hz, passive peak 276.68 Hz, played 254.53 Hz (-159.7 c from the simulator, -144.5 c from the passive peak); G: legend 392.2 Hz, passive peak 399.07 Hz, played 336.40 Hz (-265.7 c from the legend, -295.8 c from the passive peak); C+1: legend 576.8 Hz, passive peak 598.65 Hz, played 437.16 Hz (-479.9 c from the legend, -544.3 c from the passive peak). The played notes sit 1.2 to 5.4 semitones below the passive peak. The authors' own MEASURED playing frequencies are a better reference than the passive peaks (a player's notes, lips and pressure included, read from the vector Figure 13 of their paper, +-1 Hz, not a model input): their player plays 59, 83, 124 and 349 c below the first peak at G-1, D, G and C+1, and the renders at S_r 1x lie 21, 76, 141 and 129 c below those notes. The card's S_r is the value of the authors' own online simulator, and choosing it to match a player's notes would be a fit, so it is not done. The engine's reed loop was also checked against the authors' own model (their Figure 13): on plain cylinders with these reed rows it plays 48 to 173 c below that curve at S_r 0.01x to 0.1x of the earlier borrowed face 1.053692e-4 m2, and neither the reed-motion flow, the damping (Q_r 3 or 3.3), the blowing pressure (just above threshold to 0.40 Pcr) nor the closure stop (the reed never reaches it: its minimum opening just above threshold is 0.17 and 0.33 of the rest opening) is the cause. The loop does match the oscillation threshold, in pressure and in frequency, that a linear-stability calculation of the authors' stated equations gives: within 4 Hz with an engine-like bore and within 8 Hz with the authors' two-mode bore. That calculation uses the card's own reed and bore inputs, so an input misread would be shared by both. The printed curve lies 7 to 37 Hz above what those equations give with those inputs, and why is open. No printed alternative closes the gap: each one taken alone (a closing pressure of 3500 Pa for 4500 Pa, a damping Q_r of 3.3 for 3, the plus or minus 30 % bounds of the reed opening and of the reed stiffness) still leaves those equations 5.6 to 45.3 Hz below the curve over its five cylinders. The authors' own online simulator, whose code holds the card's S_r, does not close it either: its reed numbers (F_r 500 Hz, Q_r 3.3) in the paper's equations leave the threshold 5.7 to 63.1 Hz below the blue (480 Hz) and green (500 Hz) curves, and its own flow law, with a swept flow of that face, puts the threshold a further 8.6 to 21.5 Hz lower. The face borrowed from the clarinet row (1.053692e-4 m2, 2.4 percent smaller) was replaced by the simulator's, and the played notes moved by -0.6, -1.3, -1.5 and -2.1 c at G-1, D, G and C+1. The fall of the top note follows from a FITTED reed row: with the resonance of 480 Hz fitted by the authors, a reed compliance in parallel with the bore pulls C+1 down by 535 c in a closed form against 544 c rendered, and doubling S_r moves it by 92 c in the render; the same row explains only 33, 49 and 54 percent of the fall at G-1, D and G, and the rest (about 85 to 190 c below the authors' own threshold curve with the reed-motion flow taken out) is not yet explained. The authors report the same ceiling on the real duduk: the playing frequency cannot exceed the reed resonance, so Fplay < Fr for every playable note (hence Fr > 471 Hz; the fitted Fr is 480 Hz), and their measured playing frequencies of the three highest fingerings stay below their passive peaks too. S_r has no stated basis, so the page quotes its spread (clips not posted): the played fundamental at S_r 0.5x / 1x / 2x is 173.95 / 172.82 / 170.29 Hz at G-1, 258.29 / 254.53 / 247.09 Hz at D, 342.52 / 336.40 / 324.68 Hz at G and 448.74 / 437.16 / 414.41 Hz at C+1, that is -66.9 / -78.1 / -103.7 c, -134.3 / -159.7 / -211.0 c, -234.5 / -265.7 / -327.1 c and -434.6 / -479.9 / -572.4 c from the same references. Unmeasured here: the lips, the player's airway and the exact blowing pressure (the authors' reed dries and drifts 30 percent in 50 s); the pitches are what the model plays, not a tuning.
physics_present: generic fs-duct cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load carrying the paper's own bore (12 mm, 0.442 m from the reed tip) and ten 9.0 mm holes with the first k closed
the lumped single-reed owner with the authors' fitted resonance 480 Hz and quality factor 3.3, closing pressure 4500 Pa and opening 0.3 mm, driven at a fixed 0.5 Pcr
the physical baffled outlet receiver at 0.5 m on axis with the Stokes-Kirchhoff observer law and the exhaled-breath gas pack in the bore
physics_missing: the reed interior: only the Figure 6 outline, the 5.4 mm2 tip opening and two outer widths read from Figure 2 are published; the measured section b(x) of the flattened interior is the open item (bracket: Fig 6 round interior 22.07 cm3 = 250-450 c flat; linear-flattened 8.83 cm3 = 88-348 c sharp; plain 12 mm bore 11.65 cm3 used)
the undercut of the holes (none printed anywhere) and which two holes are on the back
the basis of the reed pressure face S_r (the authors' simulator's value, shown at 0.5x and 2x) and the player's lips and airway
a licensed recording of an A duduk with stated maker, key and reed to grade against: the screened clips are YouTube all-rights-reserved listening references, not committed and not posted
